name: Protobuf Encoder
description: Encode field specs or protojson into protobuf binary data, output as hex or Base64.

hints.fields: Field values are always written as strings so 64-bit integers keep their precision in the browser; bytes values need an explicit byte encoding.
hints.schema: When encoding protojson, use the field names from the .proto file or their camelCase form; 64-bit integers and bytes follow the protojson rules (string and Base64).
hints.switch: The two editor forms can be switched at any time; switching syncs the field data between them.

faq.q: What is the difference between the table and the JSON text form?
faq.a: They are two views of the same field data: the table suits filling fields one by one, the JSON text suits pasting a batch. Switching syncs them automatically.

faq.q: Why are values written as strings?
faq.a: JavaScript numbers only keep 53 bits of precision, which would corrupt 64-bit protobuf integers. Values are passed as strings and parsed by type on the server.

faq.q: How does sint32 differ from int32?
faq.a: int32 spends 10 bytes on negative numbers, while sint32 uses ZigZag encoding and stays compact. Both decode to the same number.

faq.q: How do I encode a nested message?
faq.a: Set the type to message and add child fields to that row; the children are written as a length-delimited nested message.
